ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: To illustrate the benefits of simplifying the observer's job, consider psychologist William Ickes's research on "everyday mind reading." One way he studies such mind reading is by having two strangers interact. He tapes the interaction and then has each participant view the tape. Participants are to stop the tape at different points and say what they are thinking. Then, participants see the tape again and are to stop it at different points and write down what their interaction partner was thinking at that point. Observers rate the degree to which the participant's guess about what the partner was thinking matches what the partner was actually thinking. Ickes could have had observers make their judgments on a 0 (not at all) to 100 (completely) scale. However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "similar, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using fewer categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make reliable ratings.

questions.passage: To illustrate the benefits of (A)[simplifying / complicating] the observer's job, consider psychologist William Ickes's research on "everyday mind reading." One way he studies such mind reading is by having two strangers (B)[interact / compete]. He tapes the interaction and then has each participant view the tape. Participants are to stop the tape at different points and say what they are thinking. Then, participants see the tape again and are to stop it at different points and write down what their interaction partner was thinking at that point. Observers rate the degree to which the participant's guess about what the partner was thinking matches what the partner was actually thinking. Ickes could have had observers make their judgments on a 0 (not at all) to 100 (completely) scale. However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "similar, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using fewer categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make (C)[reliable / unreliable] ratings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① simplifying - interact - reliable = 원문과 일치
❌ ② complicating(복잡하게 하는): 관찰자의 일을 '단순화하는' 것의 이점이 주제이므로 정반대
❌ ③ compete(경쟁하다): 두 낯선 사람이 '상호작용하게' 한다는 원문과 다름
❌ ④ unreliable(신뢰할 수 없는): 더 적은 범주를 사용하여 '신뢰할 수 있는' 평가를 할 수 있었다는 결론과 정반대
det.tip: simplifying the observer's job(관찰자의 일을 단순화), have two strangers interact(두 낯선 사람이 상호작용), reliable ratings(신뢰할 수 있는 평가)가 본문 핵심 표현이다.

questions.passage: To illustrate the (A)[benefits / drawbacks] of simplifying the observer's job, consider psychologist William Ickes's research on "everyday mind reading." One way he studies such mind reading is by having two strangers interact. He tapes the interaction and then has each participant view the tape. Participants are to stop the tape at different points and say what they are thinking. Observers rate the (B)[degree / frequency] to which the participant's guess about what the partner was thinking matches what the partner was actually thinking. Ickes could have had observers make their judgments on a 0 (not at all) to 100 (completely) scale. However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "similar, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using (C)[fewer / more] categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make reliable ratings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① drawbacks(단점): '단순화의 이점'을 설명하는 본문과 정반대
✅ ② benefits - degree - fewer = 원문과 일치
❌ ③ frequency(빈도): '참가자의 추측이 일치하는 정도'를 의미하므로 degree가 적절
❌ ④ more(더 많은): '더 적은 범주를 사용하여' 평가가 쉬워졌다는 원문과 정반대
det.tip: benefits of simplifying(단순화의 이점), the degree to which(~하는 정도), fewer categories(더 적은 범주)가 본문의 논리 흐름을 이끄는 핵심어이다.

det.analysis:
❌ ① researcher(연구자): 파트너가 무엇을 생각했는지 추측하는 사람은 '참가자'이지 연구자가 아님
❌ ② partially(부분적으로): 3점 척도에서 '0'은 '본질적으로 다른 내용'이라는 원문 표현과 불일치
❌ ③ harder(더 어려운): 더 적은 범주로 평가가 '더 쉬워졌다'는 결론과 정반대

det.analysis:
✅ ① rate(평가하다): 관찰자가 일치 정도를 '평가한다'는 실험 절차에 적절

❌ ② tape(테이프): 촬영 매체이며 평가 대상이 아님

Ickes could have had observers make their judgments on a 0 (not at all) to 100 (completely) scale. However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "<u>similar</u>, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using fewer categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make reliable ratings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 similar와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① distinct(뚜렷이 다른): similar의 반의어로 가장 적절
❌ ② alike(비슷한): similar의 유의어
❌ ③ comparable(비교할 만한): similar와 비슷한 의미
❌ ④ familiar(친숙한): 익숙함을 뜻하며 유사성/차이의 축과 다름
det.tip: similar(비슷한) ↔ distinct(뚜렷이 다른). 본문에서 '비슷하지만 동일하지는 않은 내용'이라는 척도 설명에 쓰인다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 actually와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 scale의 의미로 가장 적절하게 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:

det.tip: scale은 명사로 '척도/규모/비늘', 동사로 '오르다' 등 다의어이다. 본문에서는 평가를 위한 '척도'로 쓰였다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a person who watches or notices something"

det.analysis:
❌ ① participant(참가자): 직접 참여하는 사람으로, 지켜보는 사람과는 다름
❌ ② stranger(낯선 사람): 익숙하지 않은 사람이라는 뜻으로 정의와 무관
✅ ③ observer(관찰자): '무언가를 지켜보거나 주목하는 사람'이라는 정의에 정확히 부합
❌ ④ psychologist(심리학자): 전문 학자를 뜻하며 관찰 행위 자체의 정의와 다름
det.tip: observer는 'one who observes(관찰하는 사람)'으로, 본문에서 참가자의 마음 읽기 정확도를 평가하는 역할을 맡는다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① essentially different content(본질적으로 다른 내용): 3점 척도에서 '0'에 해당하는 설명으로 '2'의 자리에 부적절
